title: Mexico Has No Information or Evidence on Alleged Ties of Raúl Castro’s Grandson to Human Trafficking in Quintana Roo
author: Gustavo Castillo García
content:
_This article by Gustavo Castillo García originally appeared in the[August 11,
2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/11/politica/mexico-no-
tiene-pruebas-sobre-presuntos-nexos-de-nieto-de-raul-castro-con-trata-de-
personas), Mexico's premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. The Mexican government's Security Cabinet stated that it has
no information or evidence of the alleged involvement of **Raúl Guillermo
Rodríguez Castro** , grandson of former Cuban president Raúl Castro, with
criminal groups dedicated to human trafficking operating in the state of
Quintana Roo.

In an information note, it stated that, in relation to the report**published
by The New York Times** about the criminal network called the **" Cuban Mafia
of Quintana Roo," **the institutions of the Security Cabinet **" have no
information or evidence of their own regarding the accusations attributed in
that news report."**

Likewise, the Mexican authorities noted that they also have no information
"about the alleged links between criminal organizations and foreign officials,
or their relatives, referred to in the report."

The Mexican government reiterated "its commitment to international cooperation
in combating organized crime and human trafficking."

The US newspaper published that Rodríguez Castro allegedly has ties to an
organization dedicated to human trafficking.
